finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled `asciitrim` regex is quadratic (redos) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing markdown-it's linear native `.trim()`
evidence: Verified in packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-23 that the new `ASCII_TRIM_RE` uses the `[ws]+$` alternative with the `g` flag, and around line 134 `asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` is applied to the whole paragraph body whenever the replaced `lheading` rule accepts an underline (`---`/`===` are still accepted; only a lone `-` is rejected). That is the known polynomial-ReDoS shape — identical to the trim-newlines advisory `/^[\r\n]+|[\r\n]+$/g`, CVE-2021-33623 — since `replace` with `/g` retries at every index of a whitespace run and the greedy class loop backtracks one iteration per failed `$` test, giving O(n^2); upstream markdown-it uses native `.trim()` at this spot, so the quadratic term is introduced by this diff. It is reachable from note content any workspace member can save, and preview.ts renders synchronously via `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(...)`, so a crafted note can wedge collaborators' tabs. I could not execute markdown-it/V8 here to time the hang, so only the exploit magnitude (not the defect itself) is soft.
